claim_records.text: A Vision Transformer (ViT) is a simple neural architecture amenable to serve several computer vision tasks.
ViTs have limited built-in architectural priors, in contrast to more recent architectures that incorporate priors about input data or specific tasks.
Recent works show that ViTs benefit from self-supervised pre-training, particularly BerT-like pre-training such as BeiT.
The paper revisits the supervised training of ViTs, building upon and simplifying a recipe introduced for training ResNet-50.
The supervised training procedure includes a new simple data-augmentation procedure with only 3 augmentations, closer to the practice in self-supervised learning.

Evaluations on image classification (ImageNet-1k with and without pre-training on ImageNet-21k), transfer learning and semantic segmentation show the procedure outperforms by a large margin previous fully supervised training recipes for ViT.
The ViT trained with the described supervised procedure achieves performance comparable to that of more recent architectures.
The results of the supervised ViT training procedure could serve as better baselines for recent self-supervised approaches demonstrated on ViT.

claim_records.text: HTR-ConvText integrates a residual Convolutional Neural Network backbone with a MobileViT with Positional Encoding block in its feature extraction stage to capture structural patterns and subtle writing details.
The ConvText encoder is a hybrid hierarchical architecture that combines global context and local features while reducing sequence length for improved efficiency.
An auxiliary module in HTR-ConvText injects textual context to mitigate the weakness of Connectionist Temporal Classification.

Evaluations on IAM, READ2016, LAM and HANDS-VNOnDB show HTR-ConvText achieves improved performance and better generalization compared to existing methods, especially in scenarios with limited training samples and high handwriting diversity.

claim_records.text: Feature maps of vision encoders are fundamental to myriad modern AI tasks, ranging from core perception algorithms (semantic segmentation, object detection, depth perception) to modern multimodal understanding in vision-language models.
The current frontier of general purpose vision backbones in computer vision is Vision Transformers, typically trained using contrastive loss such as CLIP.
Most off-the-shelf ViTs, particularly CLIP, are inflexibly low resolution, running at 224 times 224px, while high-resolution versions are around 378-448px but still inflexible.

FeatSharp is a novel method to coherently and cheaply upsample the feature maps of low-resolution vision encoders while picking up on fine-grained details that would otherwise be lost due to resolution.
FeatSharp's effectiveness is demonstrated on core perception tasks as well as within agglomerative model training using RADIO as a way of providing richer targets for distillation.

In the TNT architecture, local patches (e.g., 16×16) are regarded as "visual sentences" and further divided into smaller patches (e.g., 4×4) as "visual words".

claim_records.text: When trained from scratch on ImageNet, vanilla ViT achieves inferior performance to CNNs.
The simple tokenization of input images in vanilla ViT fails to model important local structure such as edges and lines among neighboring pixels, leading to low training sample efficiency.
The redundant attention backbone design of vanilla ViT leads to limited feature richness for fixed computation budgets and limited training samples.

T2T-ViT incorporates a layer-wise Tokens-to-Token (T2T) transformation that progressively structurizes images to tokens by recursively aggregating neighboring tokens into one token, enabling local structure modeling and reducing token length.
T2T-ViT uses an efficient deep-narrow backbone structure for vision transformers, motivated by CNN architecture design after empirical study.
T2T-ViT reduces the parameter count of vanilla ViT by half.
T2T-ViT reduces the MACs of vanilla ViT by half.
T2T-ViT achieves more than 3.0% improvement over vanilla ViT when trained from scratch on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT outperforms ResNets when directly trained on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT achieves comparable performance with MobileNets when directly trained on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT with 21.5M parameters (comparable size to ResNet50) achieves 83.3% top-1 accuracy at image resolution 384×384 on ImageNet.

claim_records.text: HIRI-ViT upgrades prevalent four-stage ViT to five-stage ViT tailored for high-resolution inputs.
HIRI-ViT decomposes typical CNN operations into two parallel CNN branches in a cost-efficient manner.
Under comparable computational cost (~5.0 GFLOPs), HIRI-ViT achieves 84.3% Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with 448×448 inputs.
HIRI-ViT with 448×448 inputs improves iFormer-S with 224×224 inputs by 0.9% Top-1 accuracy under comparable computational cost (~5.0 GFLOPs).
Experiments on recognition task (ImageNet-1K dataset) and dense prediction tasks (COCO and ADE20K datasets) demonstrate the superiority of HIRI-ViT.
Existing high-resolution ViT backbones including HRViT and HRFormer still limit inputs to a small resolution of 224×224.
IRDS-a is adopted for downsampling in the first two stages with high resolution inputs.
IRDS-b is leveraged for the last two downsampling layers.
HIRI-ViT constructs three variants in different model sizes: HIRI-ViT-S (small), HIRI-ViT-B (base), and HIRI-ViT-L (large).
The entire architecture of HIRI-ViT is composed of one HR-stem layer and five stages.
For the first two stages with high-resolution inputs, HIRI-ViT replaces conventional Transformer blocks with light-weight High Resolution blocks to avoid huge computational overhead.
For the third stage, HIRI-ViT leverages only CFFN blocks to handle middle-resolution feature maps.
HIRI-ViT employs Transformer blocks in the last two stages with low-resolution inputs.
When directly enlarging Swin Transformer input resolution from 224×224 to 384×384, the top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K is evidently changed.
Simply enlarging the input resolution of prevalent ViT backbones introduces sharply increased computational costs.

claim_records.text: CrossViT is a dual-branch transformer that processes small-patch and large-patch tokens with two separate branches of different computational complexity.
CrossViT's cross-attention token fusion module uses a single token for each branch as a query to exchange information with other branches.
CrossViT's proposed cross-attention only requires linear time for both computational and memory complexity instead of quadratic time.
On ImageNet1K dataset, CrossViT outperforms DeiT by a large margin of 2% with a small to moderate increase in FLOPs and model parameters.
CrossViT performs better than or on par with several concurrent works on vision transformer, in addition to efficient CNN models.
Vision Transformer (ViT) requires very large datasets such as ImageNet21K and JFT300M for training.
DeiT shows that data augmentation and model regularization can enable training of high-performance ViT models with fewer data.
CrossViT's cross-attention module allows for linear-time generation of the attention map in fusion instead of quadratic time otherwise.
CrossViT demonstrates comparable results with EfficientNet with regards to accuracy, throughput and model parameters.

BoTNet replaced the spatial convolutions with global self-attention in the final three bottleneck blocks of a ResNet resulting in models that achieve strong performance for image classification on ImageNet benchmark.
T2T-ViT introduces a layer-wise Tokens-to-Token (T2T) transformation to encode important local structure for each token instead of the naive tokenization used in ViT.
Perceiver leverages an asymmetric attention mechanism to iteratively distill inputs into a tight latent bottleneck, allowing it to scale to handle very large inputs.

claim_records.text: With a comparable number of parameters, RetinaNet+PVT achieves 40.4 AP on the COCO dataset, surpassing RetinaNet+ResNet50 (36.3 AP) by 4.1 absolute AP.
PVT can be trained on dense partitions of the image to achieve high output resolution, and uses a progressive shrinking pyramid to reduce computations of large feature maps.
PVT serves as a unified backbone in various vision tasks without convolutions by simply replacing CNN backbones.
PVT boosts the performance of downstream tasks including object detection, semantic, and instance segmentation.
PVT takes fine-grained image patches of 4×4 pixels per patch as input to learn high-resolution representation, which is essential for dense prediction tasks.
PVT introduces a progressive shrinking pyramid to reduce the sequence length of Transformer as the network deepens, significantly reducing the computational cost.
PVT adopts a spatial-reduction attention (SRA) layer to further reduce resource consumption when learning high-resolution features.

PVT always produces a global receptive field, which is more suitable for detection and segmentation compared to traditional CNN backbones that have local receptive fields increasing with network depth.
Combining PVT and DETR constructs an end-to-end object detection system without convolutions and handcrafted components such as dense anchors and non-maximum suppression (NMS).
PVT-Small achieves 40.4 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, outperforming ResNet50 by 4.1 points (40.4 vs. 36.3) under a comparable number of parameters.
PVT-Large achieves 42.6 AP on COCO val2017, which is 1.6 points better than ResNeXt101-64x4d, with 30% less parameters.
PVT-T achieves 36.7 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 23.0M parameters.
PVT-S achieves 40.4 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 34.2M parameters.
PVT-M achieves 41.9 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 53.9M parameters.
PVT-L achieves 42.6 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 71.1M parameters.
ViT-S/32 achieves 31.7 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 60.8M parameters.
ResNet50 achieves 36.3 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 37.7M parameters.
ResNet101 achieves 38.5 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 56.7M parameters.
ResNeXt101-32x4d achieves 39.9 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 56.4M parameters.
ResNeXt101-64x4d achieves 41.0 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 95.5M parameters.
ResNet18 achieves 31.8 AP on COCO val2017 using RetinaNet for object detection, with 21.3M parameters.

ViT cannot use fine-grained image patches (e.g., 4×4 pixels per patch) as input due to resource constraints, and instead only receives coarse patches (e.g., 32×32 pixels per patch) as input, leading to its low output resolution (e.g., 32-stride).

claim_records.text: ViT-CoMer-L achieves 64.3% AP on COCO val2017 without extra training data.
ViT-CoMer-L achieves 62.1% mIoU on ADE20K val.

ViT-CoMer injects spatial pyramid multi-receptive field convolutional features into the ViT architecture, effectively alleviating the problems of limited local information interaction and single-feature representation in ViT.

ViT-CoMer proposes a simple and efficient CNN-Transformer bidirectional fusion interaction module that performs multi-scale fusion across hierarchical features, which is beneficial for handling dense prediction tasks.
ViT-CoMer is a plain, pre-training-free, and feature-enhanced ViT backbone that facilitates bidirectional interaction between CNN and transformer.
ViT-CoMer-T achieves 47.1 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 29M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
ViT-CoMer-S achieves 48.8 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 50M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
ViT-CoMer-S† achieves 52.1 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 50M parameters, using advanced pre-trained weights.
ViT-CoMer-B achieves 50.2 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 129M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
ViT-CoMer-B† achieves 54.2 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 129M parameters, using advanced pre-trained weights.
ViT-CoMer-L† achieves 55.9 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 363M parameters, using advanced pre-trained weights.
ViT-Adapter-T achieves 46.0 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 28M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
ViT-Adapter-S achieves 48.2 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 48M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
ViT-Adapter-B achieves 49.6 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 120M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
ViT-Adapter-B† achieves 51.2 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 120M parameters, using advanced pre-trained weights.
ViT-Adapter-L† achieves 52.1 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 348M parameters, using advanced pre-trained weights.
InternImage-T achieves 49.1 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 49M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
InternImage-B achieves 50.3 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 115M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
MixFormer-B3 achieves 46.2 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 35M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
PVTv2-B1 achieves 44.9 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 34M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
ViT-S achieves 44.0 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 44M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
ViT-B achieves 45.8 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 114M parameters, using ImageNet-1K pre-training.
ViT-L† achieves 48.3 AP on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, with 338M parameters, using advanced pre-trained weights.
ViT-CoMer designs two core modules: the Multi-Receptive Field Feature Pyramid module (MRFP) and the CNN-Transformer Bidirectional Fusion Interaction module (CTI).
In the weight initialization process of ViT-CoMer, the ViT module directly uses open-source pre-training, and the rest use random initialization.
ViT-CoMer-L with advanced pre-training achieves 64.3% AP, which is the best record on COCO val2017 without training on extra detection data (e.g., Objects365).
ViT-CoMer-L attains 62.1% mIoU on the ADE20K val, which is comparable with SOTA methods.
Vision-specific backbones alter the ViT structure, which prevents them from directly using existing powerful pre-trained weights, e.g., BEiT series.
ViT-CoMer preserves the original ViT, allowing it to load open-source pre-trained weights based on ViT directly, enabling rapid acquisition of enhanced generalization performance.

PVT constructs a feature pyramid structure to address the limitations of single-scale features in ViT, which simplifies the structure of the transformer and effectively reduces the computational complexity.
Vision Transformer (ViT) does not perform well in dense prediction tasks due to the lack of inner-patch information interaction and the limited diversity of feature scale.
Most existing studies devoted to designing vision-specific transformers to solve ViT's dense prediction problems introduce additional pre-training costs.

PVT constructs a feature pyramid structure to address the limitations of single-scale features in ViT, which simplifies the structure of the transformer and effectively reduces the computational complexity.
Vision Transformer (ViT) does not perform well in dense prediction tasks due to the lack of inner-patch information interaction and the limited diversity of feature scale.
Most existing studies devoted to designing vision-specific transformers to solve ViT's dense prediction problems introduce additional pre-training costs.

claim_records.text: Battle of the Backbones (BoB) benchmarks a diverse suite of pretrained models, including vision-language models, self-supervised learning trained models, and the Stable Diffusion backbone, across computer vision tasks ranging from classification to object detection to OOD generalization.

fact_fields.method: Large-scale benchmark comparison of pretrained backbones

claim_records.text: The BoB comprehensive analysis was conducted on more than 1500 training runs.

fact_fields.method: Comprehensive analysis of backbone benchmark results

claim_records.text: Among the models considered in BoB, convolutional neural networks pretrained in a supervised fashion on large training sets still perform best on most tasks, despite the increasing popularity of vision transformers and self-supervised learning.

fact_fields.method: Comparative evaluation of pretrained backbones across downstream tasks

claim_records.text: In apples-to-apples comparisons on the same architectures and similarly sized pretraining datasets, SSL backbones are highly competitive.

fact_fields.method: Apples-to-apples controlled comparison of pretraining methods

claim_records.text: BoB compares many popular publicly available pretrained checkpoints as well as randomly initialized baselines on downstream tasks including image classification on natural, medical, and satellite images, object detection and segmentation, out-of-distribution generalization, and image retrieval.

fact_fields.method: Comparative evaluation of pretrained and randomly initialized backbones

claim_records.text: Across the comprehensive BoB evaluations spanning tasks, datasets, and settings including ID and OOD, supervised ConvNeXt-Base, supervised SwinV2-Base trained using ImageNet-21k, and CLIP ViT-Base come out on top.
Among smaller backbones evaluated in BoB, ConvNeXt-Tiny and SwinV2-Tiny emerge victorious, followed by DINO ViT-Small.

fact_fields.method: Multi-task backbone evaluation at smaller model scales

claim_records.text: High-performance convolutional networks pretrained via supervised learning outperform transformers on the majority of tasks considered in BoB.

fact_fields.method: Comparative evaluation of supervised CNN and transformer backbones

claim_records.text: The observed superiority of supervised pretraining in BoB occurs because such models are often trained on larger datasets; in apples-to-apples comparisons on the same dataset scale, SSL models outperform their supervised counterparts.

fact_fields.method: Controlled comparison of pretraining methods at matched dataset scale

claim_records.text: ViTs are more sensitive to the amount of pretraining data and the number of parameters than CNNs in the BoB evaluation.

fact_fields.method: Comparative sensitivity analysis of backbone architectures

claim_records.text: Performance across tasks is strongly correlated in BoB, such that top-performing backbones tend to be universally good across tasks and settings.

claim_records.text: Vision Transformers can be interpreted as ConvNets with dynamic convolutions, enabling a unified framework to characterize existing Transformers and dynamic ConvNets and compare their design choices side by side.

fact_fields.method: Architectural equivalence interpretation of vision Transformers as dynamic ConvNets

claim_records.text: Replacing the softmax activation in vision Transformers with commonly used ConvNet modules ReLU and Layer Normalization results in a faster convergence rate and better performance.

fact_fields.method: Ablation study replacing softmax activation with ConvNet modules

claim_records.text: Following the design of depth-wise convolution, a corresponding depth-wise vision Transformer can be created that is more efficient with comparable performance.

fact_fields.method: Architectural design of depth-wise vision Transformer

claim_records.text: The equivalence between vision Transformers and dynamic ConvNets is established by rewriting self-attention as a ConvNet block consisting of static and dynamic convolutions, where query-key and attention-value matrix multiplications are regarded as two 1×1 dynamic convolutions and the scaled softmax operation is considered an activation function.

fact_fields.method: Architectural equivalence derivation of self-attention as dynamic convolution block

claim_records.text: By replacing softmax with LayerNorm and ReLU without introducing any computational cost, the top-1 ImageNet accuracy of Swin-Tiny is improved from 81.13 to 81.56.
Being S-shaped is a downside of softmax as it slows down the convergence rate compared to non-S-shaped functions such as ReLU, aligning with previous studies on ConvNets.

In the unified framework, keeping the kernel bank mechanism of Transformers and replacing the two dynamic convolutions with a single depth-wise convolution yields a lightweight vision Transformer with comparable performance.

fact_fields.method: Architectural modification of vision Transformer using depth-wise convolution

claim_records.text: Analyzing internal representation structure of ViTs and CNNs on image classification benchmarks reveals striking differences between the two architectures, including ViT having more uniform representations across all layers.
Self-attention plays a crucial role in enabling early aggregation of global information in ViTs, contributing to differences in representation structure compared to CNNs.
ViT residual connections strongly propagate features from lower to higher layers.
ViTs successfully preserve input spatial information, with noticeable effects from different classification methods.
Using CKA to compute pairwise layer similarity within models, ViTs show a much more uniform similarity structure with a clear grid-like structure compared to ResNets.

fact_fields.method: Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) pairwise layer similarity computation

claim_records.text: Lower and higher layers in ViT show much greater similarity than in ResNet, where similarity is divided into different lower/higher stages.
In cross-model CKA comparison, the lower half of 60 ResNet layers are similar to approximately the lowest quarter of ViT layers.
In cross-model CKA comparison, the top half of the ResNet is approximately similar to the next third of the ViT layers.

Even in the lowest layers of ViT, self-attention layers have a mix of local heads (small distances) and global heads (large distances), in contrast to CNNs which are hardcoded to attend only locally in lower layers.

fact_fields.method: attention distance analysis, weighting pixel distances by attention weights per head and averaging over datapoints

claim_records.text: At higher ViT layers, all self-attention heads are global.
ResNet effective receptive fields are highly local and grow gradually, while ViT effective receptive fields shift from local to global.

fact_fields.method: effective receptive field measurement as absolute value of gradient of center location of feature map (after residual connections) with respect to input, averaged across all channels per map

claim_records.text: ViT skip connections are highly influential, with a clear phase transition from preserving the CLS (class) token representation in lower layers to spatial token representations in higher layers.

fact_fields.method: representation norm comparison between skip-connection (identity) and long branch

claim_records.text: CvT improves Vision Transformer performance and efficiency by introducing convolutions into ViT via two primary modifications: a hierarchy of Transformers with a new convolutional token embedding, and a convolutional Transformer block leveraging a convolutional projection.
CvT achieves state-of-the-art performance over other Vision Transformers and ResNets on ImageNet-1k, with fewer parameters and lower FLOPs.
Pre-trained on ImageNet-22k, CvT-W24 obtains a top-1 accuracy of 87.7% on the ImageNet-1k validation set.
The positional encoding, a crucial component in existing Vision Transformers, can be safely removed in CvT without degradation to model performance.

The convolutional token embedding performs an overlapping convolution operation with stride on a 2D-reshaped token map, followed by layer normalization, enabling capture of local information, progressive sequence length decrease, and token feature dimension increase across stages.
The convolutional projection employs an s×s depth-wise separable convolution operation on a 2D-reshaped token map, replacing the linear projection prior to every self-attention block.
The stride of convolution in the convolutional projection can be used to subsample the key and value matrices to improve efficiency by 4× or more, with minimal degradation of performance.

CvT introduces desirable properties of CNNs (shift, scale, and distortion invariance) to the ViT architecture while maintaining merits of Transformers (dynamic attention, global context, and better generalization).
Performance gains of CvT are maintained when pretrained on larger datasets such as ImageNet-22k and fine-tuned to downstream tasks.

fact_fields.method: large-scale pretraining and downstream fine-tuning evaluation

claim_records.text: CvT can drop the positional embedding for tokens without any degradation to model performance, making it readily capable of accommodating variable resolutions of input images.
ViT performance is below similarly sized convolutional neural network counterparts (e.g., ResNets) when trained on smaller amounts of data.

claim_records.text: The routine of the current ViT model is to maintain a full-length patch sequence during inference, which is redundant and lacks hierarchical representation.

Hierarchical Visual Transformer (HVT) progressively pools visual tokens to shrink the sequence length and hence reduces the computational cost, analogous to the feature maps downsampling in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs).

HVT brings the benefit that model capacity can be increased by scaling dimensions of depth/width/resolution/patch size without introducing extra computational complexity due to the reduced sequence length.
The average pooled visual tokens contain more discriminative information than the single class token.
With comparable FLOPs, HVT outperforms the competitive baselines on ImageNet and CIFAR-100 datasets for the image classification task.

claim_records.text: Vision Transformers' inherent reliance on sequential input enforces the manual partitioning of images into patch sequences, which disrupts the image's inherent structural and semantic continuity.
Pattern Transformer (Patternformer) adaptively converts images to pattern sequences for Transformer input.

Patternformer employs a Convolutional Neural Network to extract various patterns from the input image, with each channel representing a unique pattern that is fed into the succeeding Transformer as a visual token.
By enabling the network to optimize these patterns, each pattern concentrates on its local region of interest, thereby preserving its intrinsic structural and semantic information.
Only employing the vanilla ResNet and Transformer, Patternformer has accomplished state-of-the-art performance on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
Only employing the vanilla ResNet and Transformer, Patternformer has achieved competitive results on ImageNet.

Gradually modernizing a standard ResNet toward the design of a vision Transformer led to the discovery of several key components that contribute to performance differences along the way.

claim_records.text: ConvLLaVA employs ConvNeXt, a hierarchical backbone, as the visual encoder of large multimodal models to replace Vision Transformer (ViT).
ConvLLaVA compresses high-resolution images into information-rich visual features to effectively prevent the generation of excessive visual tokens.
The low-resolution pretrained ConvNeXt underperforms when directly applied on high resolution, so it is updated to bridge the gap.
ConvNeXt's original compression ratio is inadequate for much higher resolution inputs, so a successive stage is trained to further compress visual tokens and reduce redundancy.
ConvLLaVA supports inputs of 1536x1536 resolution generating only 576 visual tokens, and is capable of handling images of arbitrary aspect ratios.
Experimental results demonstrate that ConvLLaVA achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art models on mainstream benchmarks.

claim_records.text: ViTs trained on ImageNet are overly reliant on local textures and fail to make adequate use of shape information.
ViTs have difficulties generalizing to out-of-distribution, real-world data.
Adding discrete tokens produced by a vector-quantized encoder to ViT's input layer is a simple and effective architecture modification to address the deficiency of over-reliance on local textures.
Discrete tokens are invariant under small perturbations and contain less information individually, which promote ViTs to learn global information that is invariant.
Adding discrete representation on four architecture variants strengthens ViT robustness by up to 12% across seven ImageNet robustness benchmarks while maintaining the performance on ImageNet.

The deployment of ViT for real-time applications is particularly challenging, especially on resource-constrained hardware such as mobile devices.
Recent efforts to reduce the computation complexity of ViT through network architecture search or hybrid design with MobileNet block still result in unsatisfactory inference speed.

claim_records.text: EfficientFormer is a dimension-consistent pure transformer (without MobileNet blocks) obtained via latency-driven slimming.
EfficientFormer-L1 achieves 79.2% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with only 1.6 ms inference latency on iPhone 12 compiled with CoreML.
EfficientFormer-L1 runs as fast as MobileNetV2×1.4 which has 1.6 ms inference latency and 74.7% top-1 accuracy.

claim_records.text: S2AFormer is an efficient Vision Transformer architecture that incorporates the novel Strip Self-Attention (SSA) mechanism.
S2AFormer uses Hybrid Perception Blocks (HPBs) to integrate the local perception capabilities of CNNs with the global context modeling of Transformer attention mechanisms.
The key innovation of Strip Self-Attention (SSA) is reducing the spatial dimensions of K and V while compressing the channel dimensions of Q and K.
The SSA design reduces computational overhead while preserving accuracy, striking a balance between efficiency and effectiveness.
S2AFormer is evaluated on ImageNet-1k for image classification, ADE20k for semantic segmentation, and COCO for object detection and instance segmentation.
S2AFormer achieves significant accuracy gains with superior efficiency in both GPU and non-GPU environments.

claim_records.text: A Vision Transformer (ViT) is a simple neural architecture amenable to serve several computer vision tasks.
ViTs have limited built-in architectural priors, in contrast to more recent architectures that incorporate priors about input data or specific tasks.
Recent works show that ViTs benefit from self-supervised pre-training, particularly BerT-like pre-training such as BeiT.
The paper revisits the supervised training of ViTs, building upon and simplifying a recipe introduced for training ResNet-50.
The supervised training procedure includes a new simple data-augmentation procedure with only 3 augmentations, closer to the practice in self-supervised learning.

Evaluations on image classification (ImageNet-1k with and without pre-training on ImageNet-21k), transfer learning and semantic segmentation show the procedure outperforms by a large margin previous fully supervised training recipes for ViT.
The ViT trained with the described supervised procedure achieves performance comparable to that of more recent architectures.
The results of the supervised ViT training procedure could serve as better baselines for recent self-supervised approaches demonstrated on ViT.

The ConvText encoder is a hybrid hierarchical architecture that combines global context and local features while reducing sequence length for improved efficiency.
An auxiliary module in HTR-ConvText injects textual context to mitigate the weakness of Connectionist Temporal Classification.

Evaluations on IAM, READ2016, LAM and HANDS-VNOnDB show HTR-ConvText achieves improved performance and better generalization compared to existing methods, especially in scenarios with limited training samples and high handwriting diversity.

claim_records.text: Modern vision systems' performance degrades remarkably quickly when presented with new tasks that have very little data, such as new classes in a classification problem or a domain shift in the input.

Neural network representations underpinning modern vision systems are subject to supervision collapse, whereby they lose any information that is not necessary for performing the training task, including information that may be necessary for transfer to new tasks or domains.
Employing self-supervised learning is proposed as a method to encourage general-purpose features that transfer better, to mitigate supervision collapse.

CrossTransformers is a novel Transformer-based neural network architecture that takes a small number of labeled images and an unlabeled query, finds coarse spatial correspondence between the query and the labeled images, and infers class membership by computing distances between spatially-corresponding features.

claim_records.text: Feature maps of vision encoders are fundamental to myriad modern AI tasks, ranging from core perception algorithms (semantic segmentation, object detection, depth perception) to modern multimodal understanding in vision-language models.
The current frontier of general purpose vision backbones in computer vision is Vision Transformers, typically trained using contrastive loss such as CLIP.
Most off-the-shelf ViTs, particularly CLIP, are inflexibly low resolution, running at 224 times 224px, while high-resolution versions are around 378-448px but still inflexible.

FeatSharp is a novel method to coherently and cheaply upsample the feature maps of low-resolution vision encoders while picking up on fine-grained details that would otherwise be lost due to resolution.
FeatSharp's effectiveness is demonstrated on core perception tasks as well as within agglomerative model training using RADIO as a way of providing richer targets for distillation.

claim_records.text: The proposed TNT (Transformer iN Transformer) architecture achieves 81.5% top-1 accuracy on the ImageNet benchmark.
The TNT architecture's 81.5% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet is approximately 1.7% higher than that of the state-of-the-art visual transformer with similar computational cost.
In the TNT architecture, local patches (e.g., 16×16) are regarded as "visual sentences" and further divided into smaller patches (e.g., 4×4) as "visual words".
In the TNT architecture, the attention of each visual word is calculated with other words in the given visual sentence with negligible computational costs.

claim_records.text: ViT-Up is an implicit feature upsampling framework that replaces external image guidance with layer-wise query construction from intermediate ViT hidden states.
On DINOv3-S+, ViT-Up improves over prior state-of-the-art image-guided upsamplers by up to +2.07 mIoU on Cityscapes.
On DINOv3-S+, ViT-Up improves over prior state-of-the-art image-guided upsamplers by up to +4.17 PCK@0.10 on SPair-71k.
With the larger DINOv3-B backbone, ViT-Up's improvement over prior state-of-the-art image-guided upsamplers increases to +3.36 mIoU on Cityscapes.
With the larger DINOv3-B backbone, ViT-Up's improvement over prior state-of-the-art image-guided upsamplers increases to +8.09 PCK@0.10 on SPair-71k.
Recent state-of-the-art image-guided feature upsampling methods that rely on shallow image encoders for guided upsampling can introduce feature leakage, fragmentation, and blur.

ViTs are commonly operated on relatively small patch-token grids due to the quadratic cost of global self-attention, creating a persistent bottleneck for dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation and depth estimation.

claim_records.text: Visual Prompt Tuning (VPT) introduces less than 1% of model parameters as trainable parameters in the input space while keeping the model backbone frozen.

VPT outperforms full fine-tuning in many cases across model capacities and training data scales, while reducing per-task storage cost.
The current modus operandi for adapting pre-trained models involves updating all backbone parameters, i.e., full fine-tuning.

claim_records.text: When trained from scratch on ImageNet, vanilla ViT achieves inferior performance to CNNs.
The simple tokenization of input images in vanilla ViT fails to model important local structure such as edges and lines among neighboring pixels, leading to low training sample efficiency.
The redundant attention backbone design of vanilla ViT leads to limited feature richness for fixed computation budgets and limited training samples.

T2T-ViT incorporates a layer-wise Tokens-to-Token (T2T) transformation that progressively structurizes images to tokens by recursively aggregating neighboring tokens into one token, enabling local structure modeling and reducing token length.
T2T-ViT uses an efficient deep-narrow backbone structure for vision transformers, motivated by CNN architecture design after empirical study.
T2T-ViT reduces the parameter count of vanilla ViT by half.
T2T-ViT reduces the MACs of vanilla ViT by half.
T2T-ViT achieves more than 3.0% improvement over vanilla ViT when trained from scratch on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT outperforms ResNets when directly trained on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT achieves comparable performance with MobileNets when directly trained on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT with 21.5M parameters (comparable size to ResNet50) achieves 83.3% top-1 accuracy at image resolution 384×384 on ImageNet.

# Original Vision Transformer and Convolutional Backbones: A Mechanism, Data-Scale, and Task-Fit Comparison

## Abstract

This review compares the original Vision Transformer (ViT) with convolutional neural-network backbones using architecture and training regime as the organizing choice. Strictly, ViT is Dosovitskiy et al.'s convolution-free patch-sequence classifier: fixed patches are linearly embedded, augmented with position information, and processed by global self-attention/MLP encoder blocks. CNN backbones such as ResNet and ResNeXt instead use local, weight-shared convolution, depth-dependent receptive-field growth, and usually hierarchical feature maps. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:abstract:claim:94f8fb4049ea] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:section:abstract:1:69b97a4ae44d:claim:9ed6923b9b67] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:abstract:claim:5c79a9124ffd] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a]

The central scientific finding is conditional rather than a universal ranking. ViT compared strongly with state-of-the-art convolutional networks and required substantially fewer training computational resources in its reported large-scale pretraining-and-transfer setting, including ImageNet, CIFAR-100 and VTAB; smaller-data training is a different regime, where cited later work says ViT remained below similarly sized CNN counterparts. Global attention also brings quadratic token complexity, and ViT's coarse, single-scale token grid is not the ready-made multi-stage interface that CNN backbones offer detection and segmentation heads. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:section:abstract:1:69b97a4ae44d:claim:9ed6923b9b67] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a] [E:arxiv:2103.10619:abstract:claim:620dfb14bc2b] [E:arxiv:2108.08810:abstract:claim:757b5d61cf31] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:abstract:claim:5c79a9124ffd] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:3:4ed8cc57457f:claim:6166499fba60] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:section:1_1_battle_of_the_backbones_the_tldr:0:34343181f775:claim:30495836476d] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:abstract:claim:94f8fb4049ea]

PVT, CvT, HVT, LeViT, ViT-CoMer and broad benchmarks such as Battle of the Backbones illuminate trade-offs but change the evaluated object or population: they add pyramids, pooling, convolutions, hybrid inference designs, modern pretraining or different task heads. Their results should therefore not be reassigned to original ViT. Across the cited evidence, CNNs contribute locality and built-in hierarchy, whereas original ViT supplies early global mixing with greater dependence on data scale; performance depends on task, resolution, model budget, pretraining and downstream interface. [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:3:4ed8cc57457f:claim:6166499fba60] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:abstract:claim:5c79a9124ffd] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:abstract:claim:219eea121636] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:abstract:claim:a671140fcb49] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:section:abstract:1:69b97a4ae44d:claim:9ed6923b9b67] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:abstract:claim:6dba2df4d842] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:section:abstract:3:547682e61b42:claim:eff216ec4dfd] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:section:abstract:5:79491ce9b36b:claim:f7bb41f9fce0] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:abstract:claim:f3405d317606] [E:arxiv:2103.10619:abstract:claim:620dfb14bc2b] [E:arxiv:2104.01136:abstract:claim:3e86efa21051] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:abstract:claim:94f8fb4049ea] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:section:1_1_battle_of_the_backbones_the_tldr:0:34343181f775:claim:30495836476d] [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012]

## Introduction

This review compares the original Vision Transformer (ViT) with convolutional neural-network backbones, using architecture and training regime as the organizing choice rather than treating every later hybrid or dense-prediction transformer as the same model. The central question is not simply which family has higher accuracy in one table: ViT replaced the conventional convolutional stack with a pure sequence model over image patches, whereas CNN backbones such as ResNet, ResNeXt, and later ConvNeXt build features through local, weight-shared convolution and typically hierarchical feature maps. The comparison therefore needs to keep mechanism, pretraining data, output resolution, downstream task, and compute or parameter budget together. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:abstract:claim:94f8fb4049ea]

The original Vision Transformer is specifically Dosovitskiy et al.'s convolution-free image-classification model: an image is divided into fixed patches, patches are linearly embedded, position information is added, and standard Transformer encoder layers process the resulting tokens. Its headline claim was conditional: when pretrained on large data and transferred to ImageNet, CIFAR-100, VTAB and other recognition benchmarks, ViT compared strongly with state-of-the-art convolutional networks while requiring substantially fewer computational resources to train. This does not establish that a randomly initialized or small-data ViT generally beats a CNN; later work explicitly reports that ViT under similarly sized CNN counterparts when trained on smaller data, citing CNNs' built-in local visual biases as a plausible reason. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:section:abstract:1:69b97a4ae44d:claim:9ed6923b9b67]

Convolutional neural-network backbones provide the reference design against which original ViT should be judged. A convolution kernel scans the image with shared weights, giving local receptive fields that grow as depth increases; ResNet's skip connections enabled very deep convolutional stacks, while multi-path designs such as ResNeXt expanded the convolutional block design space. These inductive biases suit the strong two-dimensional local structure of natural images, and CNNs were the default ImageNet-pretrained feature extractors before the rapid expansion of transformer backbones. Battle of the Backbones later found that, among the diverse pretrained models and tasks it benchmarked, supervised large-data convolutional backbones remained strongest on most tasks, although that conclusion concerns a broad modern model suite and is not a direct test of the original ViT paper's exact setup. [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:abstract:claim:94f8fb4049ea] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:section:1_1_battle_of_the_backbones_the_tldr:0:34343181f775:claim:30495836476d]

The comparison also changes with the target task. Original ViT was primarily an image-recognition architecture with a columnar, coarse patch representation; dense-prediction papers identify single-scale, low-resolution outputs and high memory or attention cost as obstacles when applying that design directly to detection and segmentation. CNN backbones naturally expose hierarchical feature maps, and transformer successors such as PVT add pyramids and spatial-reduction attention to become drop-in replacements in dense-prediction frameworks. Hybrid models such as CvT and ViT-CoMer further blur the boundary by introducing convolutions or convolutional multiscale features into transformer systems, so they are evidence for design trade-offs rather than examples of the original pure ViT. [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:abstract:claim:5c79a9124ffd] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:abstract:claim:219eea121636] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:abstract:claim:6dba2df4d842] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:section:abstract:5:79491ce9b36b:claim:f7bb41f9fce0]

## Background and Method Taxonomy

This taxonomy uses architecture and training regime as its organizing choice: first separate the original Vision Transformer from convolutional neural-network backbones, then locate later models by how much they retain each family's token-mixing, spatial hierarchy, and convolutional bias. This is a review grouping for comparison, not a universal taxonomy and not a partition asserted by the original ViT paper. It also avoids treating accuracy, efficiency, dense-prediction suitability, and multimodal use as interchangeable labels: a model can be accurate in classification but awkward as a detection backbone, or efficient at one resolution but costly at another. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:abstract:claim:94f8fb4049ea] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a] [E:arxiv:2405.15738:abstract:claim:8b6f0b7a6a17]

At the pure-CNN end, backbones compute feature maps with locally connected, weight-shared convolutions; their effective receptive field expands with depth, and common detection or segmentation frameworks consume their multi-stage pyramid of feature maps. ResNet and ResNeXt belong here, with residual and multi-path convolutional blocks respectively. The relevant comparison criteria are local spatial bias, translation-equivariant weight sharing, hierarchical resolution, and readiness for dense-prediction heads. These criteria describe the backbone family; they do not by themselves imply higher accuracy than transformers under every pretraining setting. [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:abstract:claim:5c79a9124ffd] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a]

The original Vision Transformer occupies the pure-transformer end of this grouping. It replaces the convolutional stack with non-overlapping patch embedding, positional information, a class token, and repeated global self-attention/MLP encoder blocks. Its defining criteria are sequence-wide token mixing, a columnar representation rather than a CNN-style stage pyramid, and dependence on large-scale pretraining for its strongest transfer results. Thus, “ViT” in the strict comparison means Dosovitskiy et al.'s image-classification model, not every later model with “Vision Transformer” in its name. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:section:abstract:1:69b97a4ae44d:claim:9ed6923b9b67] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a]

A second axis is task interface. Original ViT was designed for image recognition and normally produces a single-scale, relatively coarse representation from patches such as 16×16 or 32×32 pixels; PVT's authors identify this low-resolution output and the high cost of attention on large feature maps as reasons why ViT is difficult to plug directly into pixel-level detection and segmentation pipelines. CNN backbones, by contrast, are conventionally organized around downsampled feature-map stages. PVT is therefore classified as a convolution-free transformer backbone adapted to dense prediction, using fine patches, a progressive shrinking pyramid, and spatial-reduction attention; it is not the original ViT architecture. [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:abstract:claim:5c79a9124ffd] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:3:4ed8cc57457f:claim:6166499fba60]

Hybrid models form a third, deliberately mixed group rather than evidence that pure ViT and CNNs are identical. CvT introduces convolutional token embedding and convolutional projections inside a hierarchical transformer, while ViT-CoMer preserves a plain ViT branch that can load open-source ViT pretraining and adds a convolutional multiscale feature pyramid plus bidirectional CNN–Transformer fusion. Their classification criterion is which components are changed: they import locality, overlapping or hierarchical features, and multiscale reception into a transformer system. Consequently, their results should be attributed to the hybrid design and its training, not used as direct measurements of original ViT. [E:arxiv:2103.15808:abstract:claim:219eea121636] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:abstract:claim:a671140fcb49] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:section:abstract:3:547682e61b42:claim:eff216ec4dfd] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:section:abstract:5:79491ce9b36b:claim:f7bb41f9fce0] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:abstract:claim:6dba2df4d842]

Efficiency-oriented variants require a separate criterion because token reduction, hierarchical pooling, hardware speed, and parameter/FLOP budgets answer different questions. HVT progressively pools visual tokens to shorten the sequence and analogizes this reduction to CNN downsampling, whereas LeViT reuses CNN principles such as decreasing activation-map resolutions in a hybrid fast-classification network. These models may improve a speed–accuracy trade-off, but FLOPs or parameters alone do not establish latency across hardware. Likewise, ConvLLaVA's use of ConvNeXt to reduce excessive visual tokens in high-resolution multimodal models is a downstream encoder-design comparison, not a classification-backbone test of original ViT against CNNs. [E:arxiv:2103.10619:abstract:claim:620dfb14bc2b] [E:arxiv:2104.01136:abstract:claim:3e86efa21051] [E:arxiv:2405.15738:abstract:claim:8b6f0b7a6a17]

Finally, representational and unification studies should be classified as analyses rather than backbone categories. CKA comparisons show that ViTs and ResNets can develop different internal representation structures: ViT representations are more uniform across layers, while ResNet representations separate more strongly by lower and higher stages. A separate unified interpretation casts vision Transformers as ConvNets with dynamic convolutions to compare design choices and derive alternatives such as ReLU-normalized or depth-wise variants. That conceptual relationship does not erase the architectural distinction; it means locality, global mixing, hierarchy, dynamic kernels, pretraining, and task interface must be compared separately. [E:arxiv:2108.08810:section:4_representation_structure_of_vits_and_convolutional_networks:0:a15b8fa3bc59:claim:ea90270388d2] [E:arxiv:2108.08810:section:4_representation_structure_of_vits_and_convolutional_networks:0:a15b8fa3bc59:claim:02ab8c9650c5] [E:arxiv:2309.10713:abstract:claim:733cf6749238] [E:arxiv:2309.10713:abstract:claim:d87b9e51465a]

## Representative Methods

The original Vision Transformer's core mechanism is a direct replacement of the convolutional visual pipeline by a sequence model. Dosovitskiy et al. split an image into fixed, non-overlapping patches, linearly project flattened patches into embeddings, add positional embeddings, prepend a learned class token, and apply standard Transformer encoder blocks built from multi-head self-attention and MLPs. Its contribution is therefore architectural rather than a new attention operator: the paper argues that reliance on CNNs is unnecessary and that a pure transformer applied directly to image patches can perform very well on image classification after large-scale pretraining and transfer. The applicability boundary is important: this claim is about the original patch-based ViT under its pretraining-and-transfer protocol, not about every later hierarchical, convolutional, distilled, or dense-prediction model using the ViT name. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:section:abstract:1:69b97a4ae44d:claim:9ed6923b9b67]

Self-attention gives original ViT a different spatial-computation pattern from a conventional CNN. In one attention layer, tokens can exchange information across the entire image rather than only within a local convolution window; positional embeddings supply spatial order because patch tokens and attention weights do not otherwise encode absolute patch locations. This creates global context early in the network, which representation analyses identify as a major difference from ResNet-like models whose local receptive fields are initially small and expand through depth. The trade-off is that global mixing over a full patch sequence has quadratic token complexity, so fine patches or high-resolution images increase attention compute and memory rapidly. That mechanism explains why original ViT is especially effective when enough data supports learning visual relations without convolution's built-in locality, but it also motivates later token pooling, spatial reduction, windowing, and hybrid convolution designs. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a] [E:arxiv:2103.10619:abstract:claim:620dfb14bc2b] [E:arxiv:2108.08810:abstract:claim:757b5d61cf31]

The original ViT's columnar token representation should be distinguished from the hierarchical feature maps expected by many dense-prediction systems. It keeps one token grid at the patch resolution through repeated encoder blocks and typically uses the class token or global feature for classification; with common patch sizes such as 16×16 or 32×32 pixels, the spatial output is coarse relative to detection and segmentation feature needs. PVT's authors explicitly identify two obstacles in adapting that design directly to pixel-level tasks: ViT produces a single-scale, low-resolution feature map, and its compute and memory costs become high at the larger image sizes common in COCO-style detection. Thus, original ViT is best understood first as an image-recognition architecture that can be transferred, not as a ready-made multi-stage replacement for ResNet in RetinaNet or Mask R-CNN. [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:abstract:claim:5c79a9124ffd] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:3:4ed8cc57457f:claim:6166499fba60]

Convolutional neural-network backbones use a contrasting mechanism. A convolution kernel is applied across spatial locations with shared weights, creating local connectivity and translation-equivariant feature extraction; neighboring pixels are combined within the kernel, and repeated layers enlarge the effective receptive field as depth increases. PVT's review of CNN backbones describes this local-kernel structure and notes that ResNet introduced skip connections that made very deep convolutional networks practical, while multi-path blocks such as those in ResNeXt broadened convolutional block designs. These networks usually progressively downsample activation maps and expose stages at different strides and semantic levels. That hierarchy is a useful interface for detection and segmentation heads, but it is an architectural property of CNN backbones, not proof of superior classification accuracy under all training regimes. [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:abstract:claim:5c79a9124ffd] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a]

The CNN contribution in this comparison is therefore a strong set of learned and built-in visual priors: locality, weight sharing, spatial hierarchy, and depth-based receptive-field growth. CvT's authors summarize the small-data side of the contrast by noting that, despite vision Transformers' large-scale success, ViT remained below similarly sized CNN counterparts such as ResNets when trained on smaller datasets; they suggest that CNNs inherently encode properties suited to images, whose nearby pixels are strongly correlated. This does not mean CNNs always generalize better. It means that convolutional structure reduces some of what the model must learn from data, whereas the original ViT's more generic sequence-processing architecture benefits substantially from large pretraining corpora. [E:arxiv:2103.15808:section:abstract:1:69b97a4ae44d:claim:9ed6923b9b67] [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012]

The data-scale condition is central to interpreting ViT's evidence. The original paper's strongest statement is conditional: when pretrained on large amounts of data and transferred to multiple mid-sized or small recognition benchmarks, including ImageNet, CIFAR-100, and VTAB, ViT attained excellent results compared with state-of-the-art convolutional networks while requiring substantially fewer computational resources to train. Battle of the Backbones later reports that ViTs are more sensitive than CNNs to the amount of pretraining data and number of parameters, and that supervised convolutional networks were strongest on most tasks in its broad modern benchmark. These findings are complementary rather than directly rankable: the latter evaluates a diverse suite of backbones, tasks, and modern pretraining methods, whereas the original ViT claim concerns specific models, datasets, transfer settings, and training-compute comparisons. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:section:1_1_battle_of_the_backbones_the_tldr:0:34343181f775:claim:30495836476d] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:abstract:claim:94f8fb4049ea]

Representation analyses further show that the two backbone mechanisms do not merely produce the same features with different operators. CKA comparisons between ViTs and ResNets find that ViTs have a much more uniform layer-similarity structure, with lower and higher ViT layers more similar to one another, whereas ResNet representations divide more clearly into lower and higher stages. Cross-model CKA indicated that many lower ResNet layers were needed to resemble representations near the lower part of ViT, while the final portion of ViT was less aligned with the ResNet stages examined. The same analysis attributes an important role to self-attention in early global-information aggregation and to ViT residual connections in strongly propagating lower-layer features upward. These are mechanistic observations about learned representations, not evidence that one family is universally more accurate. [E:arxiv:2108.08810:section:4_representation_structure_of_vits_and_convolutional_networks:0:a15b8fa3bc59:claim:ea90270388d2] [E:arxiv:2108.08810:section:4_representation_structure_of_vits_and_convolutional_networks:0:a15b8fa3bc59:claim:02ab8c9650c5] [E:arxiv:2108.08810:section:4_representation_structure_of_vits_and_convolutional_networks:0:a15b8fa3bc59:claim:52af6f3b7abb] [E:arxiv:2108.08810:abstract:claim:757b5d61cf31]

The original ViT's residual path also changes how information persists through depth. In the CKA study, ViT residual connections were found to strongly propagate features from lower to higher layers, helping explain the relatively uniform representation structure across transformer layers. ResNets likewise use residual connections to train very deep convolutional stacks, but their stage-wise changes in resolution and channels produce stronger representational separation across groups of layers. Consequently, both families can benefit from skip connections, yet the surrounding computation differs: ViT repeats globally mixing transformer blocks on a common token sequence, while CNN backbones stack local convolutional blocks across changing spatial resolutions. [E:arxiv:2108.08810:abstract:claim:757b5d61cf31] [E:arxiv:2108.08810:section:4_representation_structure_of_vits_and_convolutional_networks:0:a15b8fa3bc59:claim:ea90270388d2] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012]

PVT illustrates how later transformer backbones borrow the task-fit properties of CNNs without becoming the original ViT. It starts from fine-grained 4×4 patches to obtain high-resolution features, progressively shrinks the sequence in a pyramid analogous to CNN stage downsampling, and uses spatial-reduction attention to control the cost of high-resolution features. The authors state that, unlike traditional CNN backbones whose local receptive fields grow with depth, PVT maintains a global receptive field and is therefore aimed at detection and segmentation; unlike original ViT, its pyramid can be inserted into dense-prediction pipelines such as RetinaNet and Mask R-CNN. PVT should thus be treated as an adapted convolution-free transformer backbone, not as evidence that the original ViT already provided the same multi-scale interface. [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:3:4ed8cc57457f:claim:6166499fba60] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:abstract:claim:5c79a9124ffd]

CvT represents a different response to the ViT–CNN comparison: it deliberately imports convolutional mechanisms into a transformer. It uses convolutional token embedding in a hierarchy of transformer stages and convolutional projections in transformer blocks. The stated design goal is to add CNN-like properties—shift, scale, and distortion invariance as characterized by the paper—while retaining transformer properties such as dynamic attention, global context, and better generalization. CvT also reports that positional encoding can be removed in that design, simplifying higher-resolution use. Its mechanism and evidence belong to a hybrid model, so CvT's ImageNet or transfer results cannot be assigned to the original pure ViT; they show that convolutional tokenization and projection can alter ViT's efficiency and inductive bias. [E:arxiv:2103.15808:abstract:claim:219eea121636] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:abstract:claim:a671140fcb49] [E:arxiv:2103.15808:section:abstract:1:69b97a4ae44d:claim:9ed6923b9b67]

ViT-CoMer is another hybrid, but it addresses dense-prediction limitations while preserving a plain ViT branch. It adds a spatial-pyramid, multi-receptive-field convolutional feature path and a CNN–Transformer bidirectional fusion module so that convolutional local and multiscale features interact with transformer features. The authors target two deficiencies they attribute to plain ViT in dense prediction: lack of inner-patch local interaction and limited feature-scale diversity. Because the ViT module can directly use open-source pretrained ViT weights while added components are initialized differently, ViT-CoMer is a feature-enhanced backbone rather than a modification that proves the original architecture was already multiscale. Its reported COCO and ADE20K results are examined as downstream-task evidence, not as a pure architecture-versus-CNN classification result. [E:arxiv:2403.07392:abstract:claim:6dba2df4d842] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:section:abstract:3:547682e61b42:claim:eff216ec4dfd] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:section:abstract:5:79491ce9b36b:claim:f7bb41f9fce0] [E:arxiv:2403.07392:abstract:claim:f3405d317606]

Hierarchical Visual Transformer addresses token redundancy rather than convolution itself. HVT progressively pools visual tokens, shortening the sequence in a way the authors analogize to feature-map downsampling in CNNs; this allows depth, width, resolution, or patch size to scale with less additional computational complexity. The paper also reports empirically that average-pooled visual tokens contain more discriminative information than a single class token in its setting. HVT is useful for understanding that original ViT's fixed full-length sequence and class-token classifier are design choices, not necessary features of all vision transformers. Its comparable-FLOP ImageNet and CIFAR-100 comparisons concern an efficiency-modified architecture and should not be read as measurements of unmodified ViT. [E:arxiv:2103.10619:abstract:claim:620dfb14bc2b]

LeViT makes the efficiency boundary even clearer by being explicitly hybrid. It re-applies convolutional-network principles—especially activation maps with decreasing resolutions—to transformer-style fast inference and introduces attention bias for positional information. Its target is the speed–accuracy trade-off in image classification across hardware measures, with the paper reporting, for example, that at 80% ImageNet top-1 accuracy LeViT is five times faster than EfficientNet on CPU. This is evidence that hierarchy, downsampling, and hybrid design can improve inference efficiency, but it is not a like-for-like comparison between original ViT and a standard CNN backbone. Hardware-specific speed also cannot be inferred from parameters or FLOPs alone. [E:arxiv:2104.01136:abstract:claim:3e86efa21051]

A unification perspective argues that vision Transformers can be interpreted as ConvNets with dynamic convolutions, placing existing transformers and dynamic ConvNets in one design framework. Under that interpretation, self-attention resembles spatially dynamic kernel construction rather than a wholly unrelated operation; the framework supports side-by-side comparisons of design choices such as softmax activation, global kernel banks, and depth-wise operations. The same paper reports two design studies: replacing softmax with ConvNet-style ReLU and Layer Normalization yielded faster convergence and better performance in its experiments, and a depth-wise vision Transformer was more efficient with comparable performance. This conceptual bridge does not eliminate the practical distinction between original ViT and static CNN backbones; it shows that some mechanisms can be analyzed as points in a shared dynamic-convolution design space. [E:arxiv:2309.10713:abstract:claim:733cf6749238] [E:arxiv:2309.10713:abstract:claim:d87b9e51465a] [E:arxiv:2309.10713:section:abstract:3:0c1521ca20ba:claim:683bed3275bc]

Modern convolutional backbones also complicate any simple “old CNN versus ViT” story. ConvNeXt is a hierarchical convolutional encoder that can serve as a visual backbone outside classification; ConvLLaVA uses ConvNeXt instead of ViT in a high-resolution large multimodal model because hierarchical convolutional compression reduces excessive visual tokens. After adapting ConvNeXt to high resolution and adding a successive compression stage, ConvLLaVA supports 1536×1536 inputs with 576 visual tokens and arbitrary aspect ratios while reporting competitive multimodal-benchmark performance. This is a task-specific encoder comparison at very high resolution, not evidence that ConvNeXt generally outperforms original ViT on ImageNet. It does, however, reinforce the importance of hierarchy and token compression when global ViT attention would face many visual tokens. [E:arxiv:2405.15738:abstract:claim:8b6f0b7a6a17]

The broad benchmark evidence should be separated from architectural mechanism. Battle of the Backbones compares many pretrained feature extractors across classification, detection, out-of-distribution generalization, and other tasks using over 1,500 training runs. Its summary names supervised ConvNeXt-Base, ImageNet-21k-supervised SwinV2-Base, and CLIP ViT-Base as top models overall, with ConvNeXt-Tiny and SwinV2-Tiny strong at smaller scales, and states that supervised convolutional networks outperform transformers on most considered tasks. It also qualifies the pretraining conclusion: when architecture and pretraining-dataset size are matched apples-to-apples, self-supervised backbones are highly competitive or better. Because this suite includes modern hierarchical transformers, CLIP, self-supervised models, ConvNeXt, and ResNet, it does not directly reproduce the original ViT-versus-CNN experiment. [E:arxiv:2310.19909:abstract:claim:94f8fb4049ea] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:section:1_1_battle_of_the_backbones_the_tldr:0:34343181f775:claim:30495836476d]

The applicability boundary for CNN backbones is therefore not universality either. Their local priors and pyramidal stages make them natural, well-established feature extractors and often strong choices when pretraining data, model size, or dense-prediction interfaces are constrained. Yet convolutional locality can also delay global integration until deeper layers, and modern benchmark winners include hierarchical transformers, language-image pretrained ViTs, and convolutional models trained on large datasets. The supported conclusion is comparative: original ViT trades convolutional locality and a built-in multi-stage map for early global token mixing and a generic transformer architecture, while CNN backbones exploit local weight sharing and hierarchy; which choice gives better performance depends on data scale, model scale, resolution, task head, and evaluation budget. [E:arxiv:2010.11929:abstract:claim:1535207f82c0] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:4:8ad541081adb:claim:138057ae0012] [E:arxiv:2102.12122:section:abstract:2:9088148f1c89:claim:c039806fc50a] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:section:1_1_battle_of_the_backbones_the_tldr:0:34343181f775:claim:30495836476d] [E:arxiv:2310.19909:abstract:claim:94f8fb4049ea]

Accordingly, the methods comparison should preserve three levels of claims. At the architecture level, original ViT is pure patch-sequence self-attention without convolution, whereas CNN backbones are local, weight-shared, hierarchical feature extractors. At the learning level, ViT's strongest original evidence depends on large-scale pretraining and transfer, while CNN inductive biases can be advantageous with smaller data. At the task-interface level, original ViT is naturally a recognition model with coarse single-scale tokens, whereas CNN stages and adapted transformer variants such as PVT, CvT, HVT, and ViT-CoMer add hierarchy, convolution, pooling, or multiscale fusion for efficiency and dense prediction. Later hybrids and benchmarks inform the trade-off, but they do not collapse the distinction between the original Vision Transformer and convolutional neural-network backbones.
